newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods leap with NYMEX, BP cracker outage.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods leap with NYMEX, BP cracker outage.

text.p: U.S. spot products leaped late Monday tracking NYMEX futures and burgeoning differentials on Gulf Coast gasoline grades spurred in part by the shutdown of a British Petroleum catcracker in Louisiana, traders said.
Gulf Coast M3-grade conventional unleaded gasoline raced about four cents a gallon higher, with bids at 1.40 cents below November futures, 1.50 cents firmer than Friday, players said.
"The immediate reason is the BP problem," one trader said, echoing reports that the company's 96,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker had been shut down.

"We've got turnarounds going right now and anything that's unscheduled tweaks the market," a Gulf trader said, adding scheduled turnarounds at Sun Co's refinery in Marcus Hook, Penn., and at Amerada Hess' refinery in St. Croix, were also lending a bullish tone.
The BP shutdown helped swell diffs on A3 reformulated gasoline about two cents a gallon, with offers at about 0.50 cent above the print, traders said.
